title: Add multi-network provisioning toggle and deterministic init sequencer for private chart
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Adds optional multi-network support and a deterministic init-job sequencer to the private Helm chart. Backwards compatible by default; new values documented in values.schema.json and README. Includes preflight probe for network readiness and safer upgrade sequencing.
description:
Summary: Introduce an optional multi-network provisioning toggle and a deterministic init-job sequencer for the private Helm chart used by the Private Installer. Motivation: customers deploying into complex VPCs or on-prem clusters with multiple CNIs (multus, secondary interfaces) needed a way to opt into additional network attachments and to ensure init jobs that prepare network-related artifacts run in a predictable order during install/upgrade. This change centralizes ordering, exposes conservative defaults, and keeps the chart backwards-compatible by default.

Design and changes: 1) values.schema.json extended with a top-level `networking` object (fields: enableMultiNetwork, attachAnnotations, requiredCNIs, readinessTimeoutSeconds). Defaults preserve single-network behavior (enableMultiNetwork: false). 2) New helper templates: templates/_network-helpers.tpl (helpers to render network annotations, validation, and templated CNI selectors). 3) Init sequencer: templates/init-sequencer.yaml implements a small set of Jobs that are annotated with `helm.sh/hook-weight` and `redwood.io/init-seq` to enforce deterministic ordering rather than relying solely on hook weight ordering. Jobs expose `backoffLimit`, `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, and an explicit `networkReadinessProbe` as an init container for network-heavy environments. 4) Preflight probe: templates/preflight-network-check.yaml added as a hook-run-before upgrade/install (hook: pre-install, pre-upgrade) that waits for required CNI plugin CRDs/endpoints and tests attachment annotations if enableMultiNetwork is true. 5) Templating: conditional logic added across templates to inject network annotations only when enabled, and to supply nodeSelector/tolerations when an onPrem profile is selected. 6) Documentation: docs/values-networking.md and README updates with examples showing Terraform variables that should be set for upstream VPC modules (subnet IDs, secondary network attachments). 7) Tests: added simple helmx unit tests (tests/helm_unit/networking_test.yaml) validating rendered templates for both enabled/disabled paths.

Checklist: - [x] Extend values.schema.json with networking block and defaults - [x] Add helper template for annotation rendering and validation - [x] Add deterministic init-sequencer job templates - [x] Add preflight network readiness hook - [x] Update README and add example for Terraform wiring - [x] Add unit tests for template rendering - [x] Run CI, iterate on review feedback

Commits summary: - feat(network): add networking values schema and helper templates - feat(init): deterministic init sequencer jobs and preflight checks - docs: add values-networking.md and terraform example - test: add helm unit test for networking disabled/enabled - fix: rename enableMultiNet -> enableMultiNetwork (review feedback)

Changed areas (high level): templates/_network-helpers.tpl, templates/init-sequencer.yaml, templates/preflight-network-check.yaml, values.schema.json, values.yaml (defaults), docs/values-networking.md, tests/helm_unit/networking_test.yaml, README.md (examples).

Review conversation (high level): - Maya Chen: "Can we avoid adding another hardcoded annotation name? Suggest we put `networkAnnotationKey` in values.schema with a sensible default so operators can rename to whatever their CNI expects." - Author (Priya): "Good point — added `annotationKey` under networking.attachAnnotations in the schema and updated helper to read from that value; tests updated." - Rafael Ortiz: "Init sequencing looks safer, but please call out upgrade semantics: what happens on rollback if a later init job already modified DB/network state?" - Author: "Added backoff+TTL and an idempotency check script (simple state file in PVC) and documented recommended canary window; also added a migration-safety note in docs." - Grace Liu: "CI failed on lint due to trailing whitespace in helpers; please run `yamllint` and helm-docs." - Author: "Fixed lint failures and pushed a follow-up commit. All CI checks green." - Maya Chen: "Approving pending one nit on naming (suggest `requiredCniPlugins` instead of `requiredCNIs`)." - Author: "Renamed to `requiredCniPlugins` and updated downstream docs/tests; resolving."

CI summary: - build (go): pass - lint (yamllint + shellcheck): pass - helm-unit-tests: pass - integration (k8s helm smoke): pass - perf/regression: skipped (non-runtime change)

Merge outcome: Merged via squash-and-merge on 2024-11-22. PR squashed into a single commit with commit message: "feat(helm): optional multi-network support and deterministic init sequencer for private chart (ENG-4221)"

Notes for operators: - Default behaviour is unchanged; to enable multi-network set `networking.enableMultiNetwork: true` and configure `networking.attachAnnotations` to the keys expected by your CNI. - The preflight job will run on every install/upgrade when the toggle is enabled; it is safe but may lengthen installs in environments where CNI CRDs are slow to converge. - Recommended Terraform wiring: expose `private.networks.secondary_subnet_ids` and map to chart values via the Helm release module. Example added in docs/values-networking.md.

Follow-ups (future PRs noted in PR body): - Add a small operator job image that can probe specific L2/L3 connectivity (ENG-4302) - Add integration test harness that runs a Multus-enabled KinD cluster (ENG-4310)
